So I wanted to come up with a system that scales a bit with level, but doesn't require an unrealistic amount of time to create something simple (like poisons) without making everything overpowered.

I based my formula off of the average times it takes to craft gear in real life, and compared that to how much an adventurer might take to do the same (http://history.stackexchange.com/questions/20833/how-long-does-it-take-to-craft-the-kinds-of-armour-worn-by-typical-medieval-warr)). My system considers the average craftsman's stats should be for their needed craft (about 13) to a hero of DnD (20).

So here it is, in a nutshell:

Find your "Work-Per-Hour" by adding the relevant modifier (like strength or intelligence), adding your proficiency bonus, and squaring the total.

Keep track of the amount of "Work" that the item needs to complete. It starts at the price (in gold) of the object times 25.

For each hour you work, subtract your "Work-Per-Hour" from remaining "Work" needed. When it hits 0, it's done!

For example, you have the burning need to craft a breastplate (400g), and have the means to make it. You're a level 9 dwarf (so a +4 proficiency) with 20 strength.

(400*25=)10000 Work

((4+5)^2 =) 81 Work-per-hour.

It will take you ((10000/81)/24=...)5 days to complete it (he IS a dwarf).

The same dwarf would need ((37500/81)/24=...)18 days to complete a full plate suit.

A toned human blacksmith who the master of his craft (+6 prof, +2 modifier) would take about 24 days, where an average human blacksmith (+4 prof, +1 mod) should take a couple months to make a full suit.

Materials cost a quarter of the value of the finished product, and you can only reliably sell things for half their original price (shopkeeper's gotta make a living, too), so you can only expect to make profit equal to the material costs.

In a nutshell:

Work-per-hour (A) = (Modifier+Proficiency Bonus)^2

Initial Work (B) = (Price *25)

For each hour you work, subtract A from B.

[EDIT] For a per-day approach, "Work-per-hour" is now "Work-per-day", where the initial work is just the default price.
